title: Clinical Guidance for Managing Fever
content: For mild to moderate fever, maintain adequate oral hydration with water or oral rehydration solutions, get plenty of rest, and wear lightweight clothing. Monitor body temperature regularly. Seek immediate medical evaluation if fever exceeds 102°F (38.9°C), persists for longer than 48 hours, or is accompanied by severe headache, neck stiffness, or confusion.

title: Headache Care and Red-Flag Warnings
content: Tension headaches and mild stress-related head pain usually respond well to quiet rest in a dim room, hydration, and stress reduction. Seek emergency care immediately if a headache occurs suddenly with severe pain ('thunderclap'), or is accompanied by slurred speech, facial numbness, high fever, or neck rigidity.

title: Managing Viral Coughs and Upper Respiratory Symptoms
content: Acute coughs following viral upper respiratory infections typically resolve within 1 to 2 weeks. Warm fluids, steam inhalation, and throat lozenges can help soothe irritation. Medical review is indicated if coughing lasts longer than 3 weeks, produces blood-stained sputum, or is accompanied by shortness of breath or high fever.

title: Emergency Protocol for Suspected Cardiac Events
content: Chest pain, heavy chest tightness, or pain radiating to the left arm or jaw is a medical emergency requiring immediate 108/112 emergency services. Do not delay emergency assistance. Resting and staying calm while emergency help is dispatched is vital.

title: Managing Indigestion and Mild Gastric Discomfort
content: Mild indigestion and heartburn can often be mitigated by avoiding large or greasy meals, remaining upright for 2 to 3 hours after eating, and avoiding known dietary triggers. Consult a doctor if abdominal pain is severe, constant, or accompanied by persistent vomiting or dark stools.

title: Guidance on Managing Seasonal Allergies
content: Seasonal allergic rhinitis can be managed by minimizing exposure to airborne allergens, using saline nasal rinses, and staying indoors during high pollen periods. Over-the-counter antihistamines should be discussed with a pharmacist or physician before starting.

title: First-Aid Instructions for Minor Injuries
content: For minor cuts, wash thoroughly with clean water and mild soap, apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding, and cover with a sterile bandage. For minor burns, cool under cold running water for 10-15 minutes. Deep wounds or uncontrolled bleeding require emergency review.

title: Safe Medication Adherence and Professional Supervision
content: Prescription medications must always be taken strictly as prescribed by a licensed healthcare professional. Never alter, stop, or combine prescription drugs without explicit medical consultation. Pharmacists provide guidance on drug interactions and proper timing.
